subject: Business
title: Design Thinking: Human-Centered Innovation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Design Thinking: Human-Centered Innovation.

hook.text: IDEO redesigned the shopping cart in just five days by watching how people actually used carts — not surveying them.

buildup.text: Design thinking starts with empathy: observe users, understand their pain points, then build solutions around them.

discovery.text: Five stages: empathize, define the problem, ideate solutions, prototype quickly, and test with real users.

twist.text: Most companies start with the solution ('we should build an app'). Design thinking starts with the problem.

climax.text: Intuit used design thinking to redesign TurboTax. Customer satisfaction jumped 20% after observing real tax-filing pain.

punchline.text: Don't build what you think people need. Watch, listen, then build.

quiz.question: What is the first step in design thinking?
options: Empathize — observe and understand users' real pain points

details.summary: Design thinking is a structured approach to innovation that starts with deeply understanding human needs through empathy, generates diverse solutions through ideation, and rapidly tests ideas through prototyping. It prioritizes user desirability over technical feasibility as the starting point.
details.whyItMatters: Most innovations fail because they solve problems nobody has. Design thinking prevents this by grounding the entire process in real human needs discovered through observation and empathy before any solution is built.
takeaways: Start with empathizing with users to understand their real unmet needs
Generate many ideas before converging on solutions to avoid premature commitment
Build quick prototypes to test assumptions cheaply before full development

faq.question: What are the five stages of design thinking?
faq.answer: Empathize by observing and interviewing users. Define the core problem based on insights gathered. Ideate by brainstorming diverse solutions without judgment. Prototype by building quick, inexpensive models. Test by gathering feedback and iterating. The stages are non-linear.

faq.question: How is design thinking different from traditional product development?
faq.answer: Traditional development starts with technical capabilities and finds markets for them. Design thinking starts with unmet human needs and finds technical solutions. It embraces ambiguity early, generates many options before choosing, and uses rapid prototyping rather than lengthy planning.
